gast-n-acurio.name: Gastón Acurio
gast-n-acurio.summary: Peruvian chef, born in 1967, credited by a 2022 study with renewing Peruvian cuisine and inspiring a new generation of Peruvian chefs.

bandeja-paisa.name: Bandeja paisa
bandeja-paisa.summary: A traditional dish from Colombia's Paisa region, typically combining beans, rice, ground or grilled meat, chicharrón, fried egg, plantain, chorizo, arepa and avocado on one platter.

physalis-peruviana.name: Physalis peruviana
physalis-peruviana.summary: A South American nightshade plant, called Cape gooseberry or aguaymanto, whose cultivation traces back to the Inca Empire and which later spread worldwide, sometimes becoming invasive.

changua.name: Changua
changua.summary: A traditional Colombian breakfast soup of milk and eggs from the Boyacá and Cundinamarca region, with a name derived from Muisca words for water and salt.

muisca.name: Muisca
muisca.summary: Pre-Columbian culture and colonial-era communities of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense in Colombia, also called the Chibcha, whose traditions lasted into the early 19th century.

colombian-coffee-growing-axis.name: Coffee Axis
colombian-coffee-growing-axis.summary: A coffee-growing region of Colombia spanning several departments, including the cities of Manizales, Pereira, Armenia and Ibagué.

lan-n-national-park.name: Lanín National Park
lan-n-national-park.summary: A national park in Argentina's Neuquén Province with diverse forests and the Lanín volcano, created in 1937.

san-mart-n-de-los-andes.name: San Martín de los Andes
san-mart-n-de-los-andes.summary: City in Argentina's Neuquén province at the foot of the Andes, founded in 1898 as a military outpost and now a major tourism destination.

crown-of-the-andes.name: Crown of the Andes
crown-of-the-andes.summary: A jewelled crown made for a statue of the Virgin Mary in Popayán, Colombia, set with 450 emeralds including the Atahualpa Emerald, said to have been seized from the Inca emperor Atahualpa in 1532.

popay-n.name: Popayán
popay-n.summary: The capital of Colombia's Cauca department, known for its colonial architecture and as home to seventeen Colombian presidents.

beatriz-gonz-lez.name: Beatriz González
beatriz-gonz-lez.summary: A Colombian painter, sculptor and art historian (1932-2026) associated with pop art, known for colorful works depicting Colombia's violent period called La Violencia.

la-violencia.name: La Violencia
la-violencia.summary: A decade of civil conflict in Colombia (1948–1958) between the Liberal and Conservative parties, sparked by the assassination of presidential candidate Jorge Eliécer Gaitán, that killed at least 200,000 people.

plaza-san-mart-n-lima.name: Plaza San Martín
plaza-san-mart-n-lima.summary: A public square in Lima's historic centre, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988, with a central monument honouring Peru's liberator José de San Martín.

fernando-botero.name: Fernando Botero
fernando-botero.summary: Colombian painter and sculptor (1932–2023) known for 'Boterismo,' his signature style of figures in exaggerated volume, and considered the most recognized Latin American artist of his lifetime.

marta-traba.name: Marta Traba
marta-traba.summary: Argentine-born art critic and writer (1930–1983) known for her contributions to Latin American art and literature.

19th-of-april-movement.name: M-19
19th-of-april-movement.summary: Colombian urban guerrilla movement active from the late 1970s through the 1980s, named for disputed 1970 elections, which demobilized in 1990 and became a political party.

palace-of-justice-siege.name: Palace of Justice siege
palace-of-justice-siege.summary: A 1985 attack in which M-19 guerrillas seized Colombia's Supreme Court building in Bogotá, holding about 350 people hostage; a military raid ended the 28-hour siege with over 100 dead.

jos-sabogal.name: José Sabogal
jos-sabogal.summary: Peruvian painter, muralist and educator (1888–1956) considered the leading figure of the country's artistic indigenist movement, which he led for around thirty years.

1939-new-york-world-s-fair.name: 1939 New York World's Fair
1939-new-york-world-s-fair.summary: International exposition held in Queens, New York, themed "the world of tomorrow," that drew over 45 million visitors between 1939 and 1940.

university-of-the-andes-colombia.name: University of the Andes (Colombia)
university-of-the-andes-colombia.summary: Private research university in Bogotá, founded in 1948 as Colombia's first nonsectarian university, teaching medicine, engineering, science, law and more.

royal-asscher-diamond-company.name: Asscher Diamond Company
royal-asscher-diamond-company.summary: A Dutch diamond-cutting company founded in 1854 by the Asscher family, still family-owned, known for cutting some of the world's most famous diamonds, including the largest ever found.

chaco-war.name: Chaco War
chaco-war.summary: A 1932-1935 war between Bolivia and Paraguay over the Gran Chaco region, the bloodiest 20th-century South American conflict, ended by a 1938 peace conference awarding most of the land to Paraguay.

gran-chaco.name: Gran Chaco
gran-chaco.summary: A vast semiarid lowland region of over one million square kilometers across Bolivia, Paraguay, Argentina and Brazil, with diverse forests, wildlife and Indigenous peoples.

ecuadorian-peruvian-war.name: Ecuadorian–Peruvian War
ecuadorian-peruvian-war.summary: A 1941 war between Ecuador and Peru, also called the War of '41, during which Peru occupied Ecuadorian territory; it coincided with but was unrelated to World War II.

el-oro-province.name: El Oro
el-oro-province.summary: The southernmost coastal province of Ecuador, named for its historic gold production and now a major banana-exporting region, with Machala as its capital.

loja-province.name: Loja
loja-province.summary: A province in southern Ecuador, part of which was occupied by Peru during the 1941 Ecuadorian–Peruvian War.

isla-de-la-luna.name: Isla de la Luna
isla-de-la-luna.summary: An island in Bolivia's Lake Titicaca, tied to Inca legend, that became a political prison nicknamed the Alcatraz of the Andes, with 30-foot adobe walls built by Paraguayan prisoners of war in the 1930s.

che-guevara.name: Che Guevara
che-guevara.summary: Argentine Marxist revolutionary (1928–1967) and major figure of the Cuban Revolution who later held key roles in Cuba's government.

ava-guarani-people.name: Chiriguanos
ava-guarani-people.summary: Indigenous people, formerly called Chiriguanos, who held their lands in the Andes foothills of southeastern Bolivia from the 16th to 19th centuries, resisting the Inca, Spanish and Bolivian states until 1892.

quechuan-languages.name: Quechua language
quechuan-languages.summary: Indigenous language family that originated in central Peru and spread through the Andes, the most widely spoken pre-Columbian language family in the Americas and the primary language of the Inca Empire.

battle-of-ybibob.name: Battle of Ybybobó
battle-of-ybibob.summary: A battle fought in late December 1934 during the Chaco War, in which Bolivia's 9th Division was surrounded and made to surrender, letting Paraguay push Bolivia out of one of its last Chaco positions.

pilcomayo-river.name: Pilcomayo River
pilcomayo-river.summary: A 1,100-kilometer river in central South America, rising in Bolivia's Andean foothills and forming part of the Argentina-Paraguay border.

hern-n-siles-zuazo.name: Hernán Siles Zuazo
hern-n-siles-zuazo.summary: Bolivian politician (1914–1996) who served as the country's 46th president from 1956 to 1960 and again from 1982 to 1985, and earlier as vice president from 1952 to 1956.

rio-protocol.name: Rio Protocol
rio-protocol.summary: A 1942 agreement signed in Rio de Janeiro by Peru and Ecuador, guaranteed by the US, Brazil, Chile and Argentina, that ended their 1941–42 war though it did not fully settle their border dispute.

cenepa-war.name: Cenepa War
cenepa-war.summary: A brief 1995 border war between Ecuador and Peru over disputed territory near the Cenepa River, ending with a 1998 peace agreement and formal border demarcation in 1999.

colombia-peru-war.name: Colombia–Peru War
colombia-peru-war.summary: Also called the Leticia War, a brief 1932–33 conflict between Colombia and Peru over Amazon territory, rooted in a 1922 treaty giving Colombia the mostly Peruvian-inhabited Leticia district.

luis-miguel-s-nchez-cerro.name: Luis Miguel Sánchez Cerro
luis-miguel-s-nchez-cerro.summary: Peruvian army officer and politician (1889–1933) who seized power in a 1930 coup, was forced into exile within months, then returned to serve as elected President of Peru from 1931 until his assassination in 1933.

american-popular-revolutionary-alliance.name: APRA
american-popular-revolutionary-alliance.summary: A Peruvian political party founded in 1924 as an anti-imperialist movement across Latin America by Víctor Raúl Haya de la Torre; later renamed the Peruvian Aprista Party.

formosa-province.name: Formosa Province
formosa-province.summary: A province in northeastern Argentina's Gran Chaco region, bordering Paraguay, Chaco and Salta, with its capital also named Formosa.

hugo-banzer.name: Hugo Banzer
hugo-banzer.summary: Bolivian politician and military officer (1926–2002) who served as president twice: as a military dictator from 1971–1978, then as an elected president from 1997–2001.

juan-jos-torres.name: Juan José Torres
juan-jos-torres.summary: A Bolivian socialist politician and military leader who served as president of Bolivia from 1970 to 1971 before being ousted in a coup; he was assassinated in exile in 1976.

indigenismo.name: Indigenismo
indigenismo.summary: A Latin American political ideology concerned with the relationship between the state and Indigenous peoples, seeking greater inclusion and recognition of Indigenous rights.

ciro-alegr-a.name: Ciro Alegría
ciro-alegr-a.summary: Peruvian journalist, politician and novelist (1909–1967), regarded as one of Peru's greatest novelists for works such as The World Is Wide and Alien.

jos-mar-a-arguedas.name: José María Arguedas
jos-mar-a-arguedas.summary: Peruvian novelist, poet, and anthropologist (1911–1969) fluent in Quechua, celebrated for his intimate portrayals of Indigenous Andean culture blending Spanish and Quechua.

c-sar-vallejo.name: César Vallejo
c-sar-vallejo.summary: Peruvian poet, writer, playwright and journalist (1892–1938), widely regarded as one of the 20th century's great poetic innovators despite publishing only two poetry collections in his lifetime.

mario-vargas-llosa.name: Mario Vargas Llosa
mario-vargas-llosa.summary: Peruvian novelist, journalist, essayist and politician (1936–2025), one of the most significant Latin American writers and a leading figure of the Latin American Boom; won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Literature.

piers-paul-read.name: Piers Paul Read
piers-paul-read.summary: British novelist, historian and biographer (born 1941) known for Alive, his 1974 account of the Andes plane crash survivors.

alive-the-story-of-the-andes-survivors.name: Alive
alive-the-story-of-the-andes-survivors.summary: 1974 book by Piers Paul Read documenting the 1972 crash of Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 in the Andes and the survivors' ordeal.
alive-the-story-of-the-andes-survivors.source_title: Alive: The Story of the Andes Survivors

uruguayan-air-force-flight-571.name: Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571
uruguayan-air-force-flight-571.summary: A 1972 charter flight that crashed in the Andes; of 45 aboard, including a rugby team, only 16 survived 72 days in the mountains before rescue.

newbery-medal.name: Newbery Medal
newbery-medal.summary: A literary award given since 1922 by the American Library Association for the most distinguished American children's literature, named after 18th-century English publisher John Newbery.

secret-of-the-andes-novel.name: Secret of the Andes
secret-of-the-andes-novel.summary: A children's novel by Ann Nolan Clark, illustrated by Jean Charlot, that won the 1953 Newbery Medal.

ann-nolan-clark.name: Ann Nolan Clark
ann-nolan-clark.summary: American writer (1896–1995) who won the 1953 Newbery Medal.

jean-charlot.name: Jean Charlot
jean-charlot.summary: A French-born American painter and illustrator (1898–1979) active mainly in Mexico and the United States.

porfirio-barba-jacob.name: Porfirio Barba-Jacob
porfirio-barba-jacob.summary: Pseudonym of Colombian poet Miguel Ángel Osorio Benítez (1883–1942), known for his many pseudonyms and years of travel and exile through Latin America.

death-in-the-andes.name: Death in the Andes
death-in-the-andes.summary: A 1993 novel by Nobel Prize-winning Peruvian author Mario Vargas Llosa, in which Civil Guard corporal Lituma investigates disappearances in a Peruvian mountain town threatened by guerrilla violence.

pishtaco.name: Pishtaco
pishtaco.summary: A folkloric boogeyman figure of the Andes, especially Peru and Bolivia, believed to extract fat from its victims, thought to originate from Spanish conquistadors' use of corpse fat as medicine.

muki-mythology.name: Muki
muki-mythology.summary: A goblin-like creature said to live and work as a miner underground, in the mythology of the Central Andes across Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia.

e-b-white.name: E. B. White
e-b-white.summary: American writer and New Yorker editor (1899–1985) known for children's classics including Charlotte's Web and Stuart Little, and as co-author of the style guide The Elements of Style.

anita-silvey.name: Anita Silvey
anita-silvey.summary: An American author and critic of children's literature, born in 1947, who edited The Horn Book Magazine and oversaw children's publishing at Houghton Mifflin.

fernando-vallejo.name: Fernando Vallejo
fernando-vallejo.summary: Colombian-born novelist, filmmaker and essayist, born in 1942, who later obtained Mexican citizenship.

pablo-landeo-mu-oz.name: Pablo Landeo Muñoz
pablo-landeo-mu-oz.summary: Peruvian writer, translator and teacher, born 1959, whose literary works are written in Quechua and Spanish.

national-university-of-san-marcos.name: University of San Marcos
national-university-of-san-marcos.summary: Public university in Lima founded in 1551, the oldest continuously operating university in the Americas, granted pontifical status by Pope Pius V in 1571.

fernando-bela-nde.name: Fernando Belaúnde
fernando-bela-nde.summary: Peruvian politician who served two terms as President of Peru, from 1963 to 1968 and 1980 to 1985, after being deposed by a military coup and later re-elected.

uchuraccay.name: Uchuraccay
uchuraccay.summary: A small village in Peru's Ayacucho region where eight journalists were murdered by villagers in 1983, prompting a commission led by Mario Vargas Llosa.

who-killed-palomino-molero.name: Who Killed Palomino Molero?
who-killed-palomino-molero.summary: A 1986 novel by Peruvian writer Mario Vargas Llosa that uses a murder mystery to examine corruption and class prejudice in 1950s Peru.

j-a-bayona.name: J. A. Bayona
j-a-bayona.summary: A Spanish filmmaker (born 1975) known for The Orphanage, The Impossible, A Monster Calls and Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom; his 2023 film Society of the Snow won 12 Goya Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director.

perito-moreno-glacier.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
perito-moreno-glacier.summary: A glacier in Argentina's Los Glaciares National Park, fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, and one of Patagonia's most visited natural attractions.

southern-patagonian-ice-field.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
southern-patagonian-ice-field.summary: The world's second-largest contiguous extrapolar ice field, straddling the Andes between Chile and Argentina, a remnant of the last-glacial Patagonian Ice Sheet.

peruvian-hairless-dog.name: Peruvian Hairless Dog
peruvian-hairless-dog.summary: A hairless dog breed native to Peru and the only indigenous dog breed still living in South America, long associated with Andean civilizations.

mario-laserna-pinz-n.name: Mario Laserna Pinzón
mario-laserna-pinz-n.summary: Colombian educator and politician born in Paris, credited with founding the University of the Andes in Bogotá in 1948 and later serving as senator and ambassador to France and Austria.

john-blashford-snell.name: John Blashford-Snell
john-blashford-snell.summary: British Army officer, explorer and author (born 1936) who founded Operation Raleigh and the Scientific Exploration Society.

pach-n-navarro.name: Pachón Navarro
pach-n-navarro.summary: A Spanish breed of hunting dog from Navarre, one of five Basque dog breeds.

council-of-rectors-of-chilean-universiti.name: Council of Rectors of Chilean Universities
council-of-rectors-of-chilean-universiti.summary: An organization founded by law in 1954 uniting the rectors of thirty Chilean public and private universities to coordinate academic standards; only its member universities receive direct state financial support.
council-of-rectors-of-chilean-universiti.source_title: Council of Rectors of Chilean Universities

movimiento-al-socialismo.name: Movement Towards Socialism (MAS)
movimiento-al-socialismo.summary: A socialist political party in Bolivia rooted in coca-grower and indigenous movements, which won repeated elections starting with Evo Morales in 2005 until 2025.

evo-morales.name: Evo Morales
evo-morales.summary: Bolivian politician and former coca growers' union leader who became the country's first indigenous president, serving from 2006 to 2019 and pursuing leftist, anti-imperialist policies.

mar-a-rostworowski.name: María Rostworowski
mar-a-rostworowski.summary: Peruvian historian (1915–2016) known for extensive, detailed publications on ancient Peruvian cultures and the Inca Empire.

benito-mussolini.name: Benito Mussolini
benito-mussolini.summary: Italian dictator (1883–1945) who founded fascism and led Italy from 1922 until his overthrow in 1943; executed by the Italian resistance in 1945.

felipe-quispe.name: Felipe Quispe
felipe-quispe.summary: Bolivian historian and political leader (1942–2021) who headed the Pachakuti Indigenous Movement and led the peasant union CSUTCB.

t-pac-katari-guerrilla-army.name: Túpac Katari Guerrilla Army
t-pac-katari-guerrilla-army.summary: Bolivian guerrilla movement founded in 1989, descended from revolutionaries trained by Che Guevara, that fought for social equality among Bolivia's indigenous population.

katarism.name: Katarism
katarism.summary: A Bolivian political movement named after the 18th-century indigenous leader Túpac Katari.

luis-a-flores.name: Luis A. Flores
luis-a-flores.summary: Peruvian lawyer and politician (1899–1969) who led the fascist Revolutionary Union party after its founder's assassination and later served as a government minister and president of the Council of Ministers.

alejandro-toledo.name: Alejandro Toledo
alejandro-toledo.summary: Peruvian politician, born 1946, who served as President of Peru from 2001 to 2006 after leading opposition to Alberto Fujimori; sentenced in 2024 for bribery.

unified-trade-union-confederation-of-pea.name: CSUTCB
unified-trade-union-confederation-of-pea.summary: Largest peasant union confederation in Bolivia, formed in 1979, which became a leading force for indigenous rights and supported nationalising the country's natural gas reserves.
unified-trade-union-confederation-of-pea.source_title: Unified Trade Union Confederation of Peasant Workers of Bolivia

aymara-people.name: Aymara people
aymara-people.summary: An Indigenous Andean people of about 2.3 million living mainly in Bolivia, Peru, Chile and Argentina, who came under Inca and then Spanish rule.

fausto-reinaga.name: Fausto Reinaga
fausto-reinaga.summary: Bolivian indigenous writer and intellectual, 1906 to 1994.

el-comercio-peru.name: El Comercio
el-comercio-peru.summary: A Lima-based Peruvian newspaper founded in 1839, the oldest newspaper in Peru and one of the oldest Spanish-language papers in the world.

nicol-s-g-mez-d-vila.name: Nicolás Gómez Dávila
nicol-s-g-mez-d-vila.summary: Colombian philosopher and aphorist (1913–1994), sometimes called the "Nietzsche of the Andes," known for critiquing modernity through short aphorisms.

falangism.name: Falangism
falangism.summary: A Spanish political ideology combining nationalism, authoritarianism, Catholic traditionalism and anti-communism, originating with the Falange Española and becoming the sole party of Francoist Spain.

mestizo.name: Mestizaje
mestizo.summary: A term for racial and cultural mixing, mainly of Spanish and Amerindian descent, that arose in colonial Hispanic America and later became a broader, positive cultural concept in Latin America.

rosario-casas-dupuy.name: Rosario Casas Dupuy
rosario-casas-dupuy.summary: A Colombian academic and former intelligence officer recruited by the CIA in Mexico City during the Cold War, arrested in 1994 for espionage, who later became a professor of literary studies and philosophy in Colombia.

pontificia-universidad-javeriana.name: Pontificia Universidad Javeriana
pontificia-universidad-javeriana.summary: A private Jesuit university in Colombia founded in 1623, with campuses in Bogotá and Cali, that has traditionally educated the Colombian upper class.

national-university-of-colombia.name: National University of Colombia
national-university-of-colombia.summary: Public research university founded in 1867, with campuses across Colombia including Bogotá and Medellín, among the country's largest and most selective universities.

friedrich-nietzsche.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
friedrich-nietzsche.summary: A German philosopher and former classical philologist known for critiquing objective truth and Christian morality, who suffered a mental collapse in 1889.

university-of-the-andes-chile.name: University of the Andes (Chile)
university-of-the-andes-chile.summary: A private, Catholic-inspired university founded in Santiago in 1989, carrying out non-profit teaching, research and community-engagement work.

aymara-language.name: Aymara language
aymara-language.summary: An indigenous language of the Bolivian Andes with over a million speakers, an official language of Bolivia and Peru alongside Spanish and Quechua.

oruro.name: Oruro
oruro.summary: A city high on Bolivia's Altiplano, capital of the Department of Oruro, whose fortunes have long risen and fallen with tin, tungsten, silver and copper mining.

pukllay.name: Pukllay
pukllay.summary: A traditional carnival festival of the central Andes; in Bolivia it is linked to Christian carnival and a battle won over the Spanish, still celebrated with Spanish-style helmets and spurs.

tarabuco.name: Tarabuco
tarabuco.summary: A Bolivian town in Chuquisaca department, known as the home of the Yampara culture and its annual Pujllay festival in March.

te-filo-cubillas.name: Teófilo Cubillas
te-filo-cubillas.summary: Peruvian footballer, born 1949, considered Peru's greatest player and one of South America's best; he starred at the 1970 and 1978 World Cups and won the 1975 Copa América.

tinku.name: Tinku
tinku.summary: A Bolivian Quechua tradition of ritual combat between communities, held especially in Potosí, that also inspired a festive dance.

cienciano.name: Cienciano
cienciano.summary: A Peruvian football club based in Cusco, founded in 1901, known for winning the 2003 Copa Sudamericana and 2004 Recopa Sudamericana.

copa-sudamericana.name: Copa Sudamericana
copa-sudamericana.summary: Annual international club football tournament run by CONMEBOL since 2002, the second-most prestigious club competition in South America.

club-atl-tico-river-plate.name: River Plate
club-atl-tico-river-plate.summary: Argentine sports club founded in 1901 in Buenos Aires, best known for its football team, one of the most successful and popular in Argentina.

boca-juniors.name: Boca Juniors
boca-juniors.summary: An Argentine sports club based in Buenos Aires's La Boca neighborhood, whose football team has won 74 official titles, more than any other Argentine club.

recopa-sudamericana.name: Recopa Sudamericana
recopa-sudamericana.summary: An annual South American club football competition organized since 1988, contested between the champions of the previous year's Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana.

alex-olmedo.name: Alex Olmedo
alex-olmedo.summary: A Peruvian-American tennis player (1936-2020) who helped the US win the Davis Cup in 1958, won two Grand Slam titles in 1959, and joined the Tennis Hall of Fame in 1987.

davis-cup.name: Davis Cup
davis-cup.summary: The premier international team tournament in men's tennis, held annually since 1900 and named after donor Dwight F. Davis.

international-tennis-hall-of-fame.name: International Tennis Hall of Fame
international-tennis-hall-of-fame.summary: A museum and hall of fame in Newport, Rhode Island, honoring tennis players and contributors, located at the former home of the US National Championships (now the US Open).
